review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. California spawning-temperature and global tagging sources support broad thermal context, but depth is a weak bathymetric proxy for this mobile pelagic species.

profile.size: Min limit 24 inches FL / Bag limit 5 per harvester / day
profile.diet: Small fish, crustaceans, squids, and pelagic prey
profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for california yellowtail.
factors.value_notes: FishBase summarizes warmer-water affinity around 18-24 °C; California yellowtail spawning off San Diego/Catalina has been reported at 16.5-22.0 °C. A 2026 Tasman Sea satellite-tagging study of adult S. lalandi found a broad 11-27 °C thermal envelope and core use around 17.4-20.8 °C, but that population is geographically distinct. These sources support broad thermal context, not a universal California SST catch curve or validation of the configured 16-25 °C / 19-23 °C intervals.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for california yellowtail.
factors.value_notes: California yellowtail is a mobile benthopelagic/pelagic fish using coastal and oceanic waters, reefs, kelp beds and offshore islands; sources report dives or occurrence well beyond 50 m, including up to 228 m. The runtime variable is seafloor bathymetric depth, not fish vertical depth. A 0-50 m band is only a weak nearshore/reef-context proxy and does not represent the species' full offshore habitat; numeric values remain unchanged.
